Rowan, when people say a city is cracking down, what does that actually look like?
Most of it comes down to a few tools.

A principal residence rule, meaning you can only rent out the home you actually live in.
Sometimes a cap on nights.
Fines.
And more and more, the platforms themselves have to check numbers and take listings down.
Start close to home.
Nova Scotia.
Nova Scotia has a provincial registry.
If you rent a place for twenty eight days in a row or less, you have to register before you operate.
That covers short term rentals and traditional places like B and Bs, cottages, even yurts.
Each location needs its own registration number, and you renew every year by April first.
Say someone buys a cottage this fall that the last owner already rented out.
Can they keep using that number?
No.
The province says a registration can't be transferred to a new owner.
The new owner has to register before operating.
